query_text: How do you create eye contact with someone with a lazy eye?

message.content:
Based on my search, I found helpful information about creating eye contact with someone who has a lazy eye (amblyopia or strabismus). Here are the key strategies:

## General Eye Contact Strategies That Apply

Many of the same principles for comfortable eye contact apply when interacting with someone who has a lazy eye:

**Look at the person's face broadly rather than focusing intensely on one eye.** The "triangle technique" is particularly useful—imagine an inverted triangle connecting both eyes and the mouth, and rotate your gaze between these three points every few seconds. This prevents staring at one eye and feels more natural for both parties.

**Look near the eyes if direct eye contact feels uncomfortable.** As one source notes, "If looking someone directly in the eyes is too stressful, instead look at a spot on their nose, mouth, or chin." For someone with a lazy eye, looking at the bridge of the nose or forehead can help you appear engaged without creating tension.

**Use the 50/70 rule.** Maintain eye contact about 50% of the time when speaking and 70% when listening, holding for 4-5 seconds at a time before glancing away naturally.

## Specific Considerations for Lazy Eye

**Focus on the person, not the condition.** Adults with lazy eye often experience self-consciousness and may have faced misunderstanding in social situations. The key is to be natural and not draw attention to their eye alignment.

**Let your eyes go slightly out of focus.** This technique "has the added benefit of softening and relaxing your gaze" and can help you take in the person's whole face rather than fixating on which eye is looking where.

**Be patient and culturally sensitive.** Some individuals may have developed different comfort levels with eye contact due to their vision condition or related social experiences.

**Break gaze naturally.** Make gestures, nod, or look away slowly rather than darting your eyes, which can signal discomfort. This is especially important so the person doesn't feel you're avoiding them because of their eye.

## The Most Important Principle

The search results emphasize that building trust and making the person feel comfortable is paramount. Rather than worrying about "which eye to look at," focus on being present and engaged in the conversation. The person with lazy eye will likely appreciate your natural, respectful approach far more than any technical eye-contact perfection.

4. https://www.meyeclinic.co.il/en/article/lazy-eye-and-keratoconus/
5. https://www.verywellmind.com/how-do-i-maintain-good-eye-contact-3024392
